title: Add Homebrew formula for open-source cmdrvl umbrella CLI once published
description:
## Background
Once the open-source `cmdrvl` umbrella porcelain CLI (`cmdrvl capabilities --json`, `cmdrvl doctor`, `cmdrvl inspect`, `cmdrvl diff`, `cmdrvl receipt`) cuts its first release, users and agents should be able to install the whole workflow entry point with a single `brew install cmdrvl/tap/cmdrvl`.

## Deliverables
- Add `Formula/cmdrvl.rb` with macOS/Linux arm64/x86_64 bottles and SHA-256 verification.
- Document whether `cmdrvl` depends on individual spine formulae or bundles/manages them, with `test do` verifying `cmdrvl --version` and `cmdrvl capabilities --json`.
acceptance_criteria: brew install cmdrvl/tap/cmdrvl installs cleanly and passes brew test cmdrvl/tap/cmdrvl.

title: Add bin/spine-doctor shell script for pipeline health checks
description:
## Problem

There is no way to verify the spine pipeline is correctly installed and wired. After installing 7+ tools from the tap, a user (or agent) has to manually run each binary to check it exists, then mentally reconstruct the pipeline order from individual --describe outputs.

During the spring11 CRE extraction session, we discovered:
- \`profile --describe\` crashes (exit 2, "Failed to read operator.json")
- \`rvl\` is missing --describe, --schema, and --version entirely
- \`fingerprint --describe\` returns a different schema format than the rest
- The binary name (\`hashbytes\`) doesn't match the describe name (\`hash\`) or the formula name (\`cmdrvl-hash\`)

None of this was obvious until we tried each tool individually.

## Proposal

A shell script at \`bin/spine-doctor\` that:

1. Checks each known binary exists on PATH
2. Runs \`<tool> --version\` and reports version (or flags failure)
3. Runs \`<tool> --describe\` and flags failures or non-standard output
4. Assembles and prints the pipeline DAG from \`pipeline.upstream/downstream\`
5. Flags naming inconsistencies (binary vs describe name)
6. Reports an overall health status

Example output:
\`\`\`
spine-doctor

Tools:
  vacuum     0.1.0  ✓ describe ✓ schema
  hashbytes  0.2.0  ✓ describe ✓ schema  ⚠ name mismatch (describe: "hash")
  fingerprint 0.3.0 ⚠ describe (non-standard schema)  ✓ schema
  shape      0.2.0  ✓ describe  ✗ schema (not supported)
  profile    0.1.0  ✗ describe (exit 2)  ✓ schema
  rvl        ???    ✗ describe  ✗ schema  ✗ version
  lock       0.2.0  ✓ describe ✓ schema
  canon      (not installed)
  pack       (not installed)

Pipeline:
  vacuum → hashbytes → fingerprint → lock
                    ↘ shape → rvl
           profile ─────────→ (shape, rvl) [deferred in v0]

Health: 5/9 tools installed, 2 with --describe issues, 1 missing --version
\`\`\`

## Implementation notes

- Pure shell script, no dependencies beyond the tools themselves
- The tap already defines the canonical formula list — derive tool names from Formula/*.rb
- Could also check witness ledger health (\`~/.epistemic/witness.jsonl\` exists and is writable)
- Keep it simple: if it grows beyond ~100 lines, graduate to a real binary in its own repo
notes: Dependency note: spine-doctor will report issues that are being fixed in parallel (bd-25h rvl --describe, bd-1c4 profile --describe, bd-3mz fingerprint operator.v0, bd-1e0 hash naming). Implement after those fixes land for accurate baseline reporting. Consider P3 until prerequisites are done.
close_reason: Added bin/spine-doctor — checks all 9 tools for PATH presence, --version, --describe (operator.v0), --schema, name mismatches, and witness ledger health. 95 lines of pure bash, no external deps.

title: Resolve cmdrvl-hash / cmdrvl-benchmark formula naming friction and add tap README with verified install commands
description:
## Background & Evidence
Org docs (`cmdrvl/.github` README, `SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`, `AGENT_PROMPT.md`) tell users and agents to run `brew install cmdrvl/tap/hash` and `brew install cmdrvl/tap/benchmark` (and claim the latter installs `cmdrvl-benchmark`). In reality, `homebrew-tap` ships `Formula/cmdrvl-hash.rb` (installing `hashbytes`) and `Formula/cmdrvl-benchmark.rb` (installing `benchmark`). First-try installs fail immediately.

## Goal
Eliminate Homebrew installation friction and drift between formulae, installed binaries, and org documentation.

## Deliverables
- Add a clear `README.md` in `homebrew-tap` listing every formula, installed binary name, and verified copy-paste `brew install` commands (core set + full set).
- Decide and document Homebrew aliases or caveats for `cmdrvl-hash` (`hashbytes`) and `cmdrvl-benchmark` (`benchmark`), plus verify `vacuum.rb` documents its second installed binary `s3-to-vacuum`.
- Add a CI check verifying every formula passes `brew audit --strict` (or Ruby syntax + binary-name consistency check) and matches the tap README table.
acceptance_criteria: Tap README documents exact formula->binary mappings, caveats clarify hashbytes/benchmark/s3-to-vacuum, and CI validates formula table parity.
close_reason: Verified by independent verifier at eb18ee1 (git-archive extract): ruby -c on all Formula/*.rb, bin/check-tap, tests/check_tap_test.rb clean; ruby bin/check-tap = 16 formulae checked (syntax, binary mappings, 2 aliases, README install commands); ruby tests/check_tap_test.rb = 10 runs 0 failures; checker is local-only, no network/install. Formula->binary mapping cmdrvl-hash->hashbytes, cmdrvl-benchmark->benchmark, vacuum->vacuum+s3-to-vacuum agrees with README; caveats added to all 3 formulae; check-tap.yml runs both scripts. Scope: tap files only. Not verified: brew audit/install, alias resolution inside Homebrew (agent also disclosed).
